additional_info.subject: RE: ID0410800-DC/Si-D/AT-[Y2 / S8 313854599002]Connection Interruption from XF3+ Charging Not possible+ Serial no is wrong in SCB) CRM:00798001965
additional_info.body:
Hello
Johannes,
Hope you are doing well.
Please find the answers to your queries below:
We have updated the serial number
Y2 / S8 313854599002
on SCB as per the serial number printed on the charger’s nameplate.
As per the previous ticket
0394049
, the CFast was to be reflash. Could you please confirm if this activity has been completed? If yes, the ticket can be closed. Additionally, we can refer the logs below.
3.As we checked the signal strength in the logs, it shows poor signal strength. Due to this marginal data with drop-outs is possible, and performance will drop drastically.
Please consider the following points that may cause the charger to trip the SCB.
The data service of a mobile network operator may be unavailable.
- SIM card disabled / expired
- Monthly data volume exhausted
- Signal strength got weak due to changed radio transmission conditions
- In case of M2M contracts is IP not enabled
Backend related issues
- Backend changed the settings for the affected charger
- OCPP server on Backend side unavailable
Teltonika related issues
- Router switches to a wrong network service (e.g. 3G instead of 4G)
- Hardware failure of Router
- Router software crash
4.Based on the video shared in the Webform, we checked the logs for the given timestamp, where it is found that the EV SOC was 100% during the session start & due to the session was terminated.
If you have any further query, please do notify us.
Regards,
Beerpal Singh
eMobility Support
Please do not change the subject line with replying back to this email.

additional_info.subject: RE: AW: ID0410800-DC/Si-D/AT-[Y2 / S8 313854599002]Connection Interruption from XF3+ Charging Not possible+ Serial no is wrong in SCB) CRM:00798001965
additional_info.body:
Hello Johannes,
Thanks for the response.
We stated in the previous mail regarding the ticket (#0394049) that the issue was reported, and it has now been resolved. We have attached the firmware update history logs also in the previous mail. You may now close ticket #0394049 as the issue is resolved.
Based on the logs and the time mentioned in the shared video in the Webform, we found that the EV was at 100% SOC (battery full) when the charging session started. Energy management reason at EV, e.g. battery is full or charging is scheduled to start at a later point in time. Simultaneously, EvRequestedCurrent will be set to 0. It should be understood that, according to IEC61851-1, the only 'master' in this process is the "EV".
If this answers your query, shall we proceed and close the ticket?
Regards,
Beerpal Singh
eMobility Support
Please do not change the subject line with replying back to this email.
